clue.text: Judiciary, although peevish, displays its independence

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: the crossbenches are where independent peers sit

parts.note: peevish means cross, irritable
the bench is the collective term for judges and magistrates

explanation.surface: Even a judge in a bad mood shows that the courts stand apart from government.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossbenches in the House of Lords seat peers who belong to no party, so the definition describes what sitting there shows rather than naming the seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossbench members of the House of Lords are unaffiliated, so the word stands for political independence.

clue.text: "Mistress. of herself though — fall" (Pope)

parts.note: a line from Pope's Moral Essays praising a woman who stays calm even when her fine porcelain breaks

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the missing word in Pope's line is the porcelain whose fall the lady bears calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain ware is named after the country it first came from.

clue.text: Alert; like the collapsed scrum.?

definitions.meaning: when a rugby scrum collapses the players end up lying on top of the ball

explanation.surface: A rugby report notes the forwards were sharp despite their scrum falling over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sharp and quick-witted is said to be 'on the ball', and a collapsed scrum literally lies on it.

clue.text: Inadequate penalty for German bomber pilots who were

definitions.text: Inadequate penalty for German bomber pilots who were

parts.words: Inadequate penalty for German bomber pilots who were
parts.note: the Luftwaffe bombed Coventry in 1940; the phrase also means being shunned, a feeble punishment for that

explanation.walkthrough: To be sent to Coventry is to be ostracised; for the pilots who flew to bomb that English city, it was literally where they had been sent.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being deliberately ignored by everyone, a mild punishment compared with the raid itself.

clue.text: Made certain it endures

annotationWithheld.why: Made certain it endures (7): 'Made certain' defines ENSURED and 'endures' holds its letters, but no clue word signals the anagram; the only candidate, 'Made', is already in the definition, so it would do two jobs

clue.text: Pressing needs for cricketers

parts.note: ironing trousers puts folds in them, and a cricket batsman needs the line marked on the pitch to stand behind

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the crease is the white line marking where the batsman and bowler stand; 'Pressing' looks like urgent but is ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing presses folds into cloth, and the lines painted on a cricket pitch share that name.

clue.text: Any old iron in the planetarium

definitions.text: Any old iron in the planetarium

parts.words: Any old iron in the planetarium
parts.note: alchemists named iron after a planet, so the old name for the metal is also a body shown in a planetarium

explanation.walkthrough: 'Any old iron' was the cry of the British scrap-metal collector; here 'old iron' is iron under its old alchemical name, which is also the name of a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Alchemy linked each metal to a planet, and iron's planet was the red one named after the Roman god of war.

clue.text: Locke's place in Hampshire

parts.note: ... Locke is a Charles Kingsley novel, and the hero's first name is also a market town in Hampshire

explanation.walkthrough: Locke is not the philosopher but Kingsley's hero Alton Locke; Hampshire is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of Kingsley's tailor-poet is shared with a Hampshire town famous for brewing.

clue.text: The team takes measures and avoids the issue

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
steps are measures taken, actions

explanation.surface: A club takes action while dodging the real question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins SIDE and STEPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidestep a question is to evade it, as a dancer or runner moves aside.

clue.text: Was young Washington so bound over to keep the peace?

definitions.text: Was young Washington so bound over to keep the peace?

parts.words: Was young Washington so bound over to keep the peace
parts.note: the boy George Washington, of the cherry-tree story, cut it with a hatchet, so a court might have ordered him to hide the tool away

explanation.walkthrough: 'bound over to keep the peace' is a British court order to behave; the idiom for making peace literally means putting the young Washington's tool in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To make peace after a quarrel is to bury the tomahawk, an idiom from Native American custom.

clue.text: For what purposes are campers found here ?

definitions.text: For what purposes are campers found here ?

parts.words: For what purposes are campers found here
parts.note: read as two words, the answer says where campers sleep; read as one, it means aims

explanation.walkthrough: Split after two letters the word gives the place campers are found; whole, it is a synonym of 'purposes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Intents are aims or purposes, the pair joined in the phrase 'to all intents and purposes'.

clue.text: Rejoiced in de luxe return round the square

indicators.note: the turned-round letters go round the square's letter, holding it inside
a return goes back the way it came, so de luxe is written from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's square, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: Someone delighted in a luxurious trip home around the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns DELUXE into EXULED, and 'round' puts it round T, from T-square, giving EXUL-T-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To exult is to rejoice triumphantly, so the past tense matches 'rejoiced'.

clue.text: Purest are involved in providing openings

indicators.note: involved means twisted or tangled up, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: The purest people take part in giving opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges the nine letters of PUREST ARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Apertures are holes or gaps, as in a camera's lens opening.

clue.text: No Southerners among these jerks!

definitions.meaning: in the American Civil War the Yankees were the Northerners, so no Southerner is one
jerks as a verb means pulls sharply, tugs

explanation.surface: A complaint that none of these idiots comes from the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' looks like an insult but is the verb: to yank is to jerk.
explanation.definitionFit: Yankees were the Union side, the North; and a yank is a sudden tug.

clue.text: Free cash abroad

parts.note: a foreign currency whose name, said out loud, is the word for free or candid, as in free speech

explanation.walkthrough: The currency of France (and Switzerland) is pronounced like 'frank', meaning free or outspoken.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the French unit of money, so it is cash used abroad, and its name sounds like a word meaning open or unrestrained.

clue.text: Like Fido's capacity (with sugar on his nose ?)

definitions.text: Like Fido's capacity (with sugar on his nose ?)

parts.words: Like Fido's capacity (with sugar on his nose
parts.note: a dog balancing a lump of sugar on its nose waits for the word 'trust', so his role is one held in trust

explanation.walkthrough: The trick of a dog holding sugar on its nose until told 'trust' gives a capacity held in trust; the dog's name Fido is Latin for 'I trust'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiduciary capacity is a position of trust, from Latin fiducia, trust.

clue.text: Pluto leads the advance with an explosive performance

indicators.note: Pluto leads, going in front of the word for the advance

parts.note: Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
a charge is an attacking advance, as by cavalry

explanation.surface: The god of the underworld heads an attack in a show of fireworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluto' wants to be the planet; it is the god, also called Dis.
explanation.definitionFit: The firing of a gun or a blast is a discharge, an explosive release.

clue.text: Has kittens again ? That brightens things up !

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
a cat that kindles gives birth to a litter

explanation.surface: A cat produces another litter, which cheers the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kindle' is an old word for a cat giving birth; it also means to set alight, so rekindling brightens.
explanation.definitionFit: To light again is to bring back brightness, as when a fire is relit.

clue.text: " There are many events in the womb of time which will be" (Othello)

definitions.text: " There are many events in the womb of time which will be" (Othello)

parts.words: " There are many events in the womb of time which will be" (Othello)
parts.note: Iago's line in Othello, Act 1, ends with the word that completes the image of the womb giving birth

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the solver supplies the missing last word of Iago's line, which carries on the birth image.
explanation.definitionFit: Events in the womb of time will be born, that is brought forth, in due course.

clue.text: Song in part of the woodwind is broadcast once more

indicators.note: the song is placed inside the woodwind part

parts.note: a reed is the vibrating part of an oboe, clarinet or bassoon
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A tune played in the woodwind section goes out on air again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of the woodwind' looks like a hidden-word signal, but it is a synonym: the vibrating reed of an oboe or clarinet.
explanation.definitionFit: To relay is to pass on a broadcast, retransmitting it.

clue.text: "My right there is none to" (Cowper)

parts.note: from Cowper's verses on Alexander Selkirk, 'I am monarch of all I survey', which end the line with a word for challenge

explanation.walkthrough: A quotation clue: the solver completes Cowper's line about the castaway Selkirk, monarch of his island.
explanation.definitionFit: To contest or challenge a claim is to question it, so no one can challenge his right.

clue.text: Packs up on these walks

parts.note: on long country walks the walkers carry rucksacks on their backs, packs up

explanation.walkthrough: 'Packs up' looks like giving up; it means rucksacks carried up on the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Long walks in the country are rambles where walkers carry packs.

clue.text: This letter in the mail ?

parts.note: a letter sent on to be copied by each recipient, and also the linked metal of armour called mail

explanation.walkthrough: 'mail' is both the post and armour; the word makes a kind of letter with the first and a kind of mail with the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain letter is passed on through the post, and chain mail is armour of linked rings.

clue.text: It's all over nothing, one discovers here

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the following ones

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
a means one

explanation.surface: Something that is complete over nothing, a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLOA is a town in central Scotland; 'here' is the definition, the place the solver discovers.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to a place, and Alloa is a Scottish town on the Forth.

clue.text: Land of Camoens

parts.note: Camoens, the national poet of Portugal, wrote the Lusiads, named after the old Roman province

explanation.walkthrough: Camoens is Portugal's national poet; the answer is the Roman name for Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman province covered most of modern Portugal, the poet's homeland.

clue.text: I pass awkward point in orbit

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily skips a spot on their trajectory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges I PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An apsis is the nearest or farthest point of a body's path round another, an astronomy term.

clue.text: Hypersensitivity displayed in the gallery

indicators.note: the letters of gallery are laid out and shown in a different order

explanation.surface: Overreaction is put on show in the art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed in' looks like a hidden-word signal, but no run of 'the gallery' gives the answer; 'displayed' rearranges GALLERY.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergy is the body overreacting to a harmless substance such as pollen.

clue.text: Out of bed, coming to grips with supports

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
grips as a noun means holds, as in wrestling

explanation.surface: Just risen, someone gets to grips with their braces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to grips with' looks like one phrase; the link 'coming to' joins UP and HOLDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold is to support or maintain, as a court upholds a ruling.

clue.text: Time for assent ? Right

parts.note: yea is an old word of assent, yes

explanation.surface: A question of whether it is time to agree, answered with a firm yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelvemonth is a period of time.

clue.text: Is in commercial business

parts.note: to be engaged in making commercials, publicity for products

explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial' means a TV or radio promotion, not trade: whoever is in that business promotes goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To publicise a product in paid notices is what a firm does in commercials.
